record.original_question: Let U be a connected open set in Rn . Brelot and Choquet [113] showed that the set of points on the boundary of U which are accessible from the interior by (finite length) rectifiable paths supports harmonic measure. It is natural, in view of polygonal path connectedness of finely open sets, to ask if the same is true for finely open sets and the Keldysh measure. (T. Lyons and B. Øksendal)

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Background. Let $U$ be a (Euclidean) open set in $\mathbb{R}^n$, $n\ge 2$. A point $x\in\partial U$ is said to be accessible from the interior by a rectifiable path if there exists a continuous map $\gamma:[0,1]\to\overline{U}$ of finite length such that $\gamma([0,1))\subset U$ and $\gamma(1)=x$. A classical theorem states that, when $U$ is connected and open in the Euclidean sense, the set of boundary points accessible by rectifiable paths carries full harmonic measure (relative to any pole in $U$).

Now consider the fine topology on $\mathbb{R}^n$, namely the coarsest topology making every superharmonic function on $\mathbb{R}^n$ continuous. Let $U\subset\mathbb{R}^n$ be a finely open and finely connected set. For $x\in U$, the Keldysh measure $\mu_x$ on the fine boundary $\partial_f U$ is the swept-out (balayage) measure that represents finely harmonic functions on $U$ via boundary integration:
$$h(x)=\int_{\partial_f U} h^*\,d\mu_x$$
for bounded finely harmonic $h$ on $U$ with appropriate fine boundary values $h^*$.

A finely open connected set is known to be polygonally path-connected (in fact, by finite-length polygonal paths whose interior lies in $U$ except at endpoints, in a suitable sense). Call a point $x\in\partial_f U$ rectifiably accessible from $U$ if there is a path $\gamma:[0,1]\to\mathbb{R}^n$ of finite Euclidean length with $\gamma([0,1))\subset U$ and $\gamma(1)=x$.

Question. Does the set of rectifiably accessible points of $\partial_f U$ support the Keldysh measure $\mu_x$ for every $x\in U$? Equivalently, is $\mu_x$ concentrated on the set of fine boundary points of $U$ that can be reached from $U$ by paths of finite length?
artifact.category_tag: Fine potential theory and Keldysh measure
artifact.status_search_result: A web search did not surface a published resolution of the question whether the rectifiably accessible part of the fine boundary of a finely open connected set carries the Keldysh measure. Related work on analytic capacity and differentiability of finely harmonic functions exists, but no result confirming or refuting the rectifiable-path support property for Keldysh measure was located.

status_evidence.title: Analytic capacity and differentiability properties of finely harmonic functions
status_evidence.snippet: Work by T. J. Lyons and related authors on finely harmonic functions and analytic capacity, but does not address the Keldysh-measure rectifiable accessibility question directly.
status_evidence.claim: No direct resolution of the rectifiable-accessibility/Keldysh-measure question found.

status_evidence.title: The Choquet and Kellogg properties for the fine topology
status_evidence.snippet: Studies fine-topology properties relevant to potential theory but does not resolve the stated problem.
